title: Jambavan knows his Lord
hook: a jewel goes missing, a rumor blames Krishna, and a bear in a cave knows him from long ago
carry: one Lord, come again as Rama and Krishna
tomorrow: what can a poor man bring the richest friend he has?

segments.voice: Yesterday: Rukmini's letter, and shravana, devotion that begins by hearing, then chooses.
screen: `THE TENTH BOOK, CONTINUED.` · `I HAVE HEARD. I HAVE CHOSEN.`

segments.voice: Someone is walking toward Dwaraka so bright that people in the streets shield their eyes. They run to Krishna: the sun god himself is coming to see you! Krishna laughs. It isn't the sun, he tells them. It's Satrajit, wearing his jewel. The jewel is the Syamantaka, a gift to Satrajit from the sun. It's beautiful, and it brings wealth to whoever keeps it. Before long, it will go missing. And the city will start whispering a name. Krishna's.
screen: `IS THE SUN COMING?` → `NO: SATRAJIT AND HIS JEWEL.` → `THE CITY WHISPERS A NAME.`

segments.voice: Here's how it goes wrong, in paraphrase. Krishna asks Satrajit to give the jewel to the king, Ugrasena. Satrajit refuses. Not long after, his brother Prasena wears it out hunting and doesn't come back. A lion kills him and takes the jewel; then a bear kills the lion and carries it to his cave. The people of Dwaraka only know that Krishna asked for the jewel, and now it's gone. So people talk. Krishna doesn't argue; he goes and finds out. He follows the trail to a dark cave and goes in alone. The bear is Jambavan, the bear king who served Rama in the Ramayana, ages before. They fight in the dark, on and on, until Jambavan realizes that no one but his own Lord could be this strong. It's Rama, come again in a new form. He bows, gives up the jewel, and gives his daughter Jambavati in marriage too. Back in Dwaraka, Krishna returns the jewel before everyone, and Satrajit, ashamed, gives him his daughter Satyabhama. Now the teaching inside that cave. Hindus call it avatara: God coming down into the world. In the Gita, Krishna says that whenever dharma falls and wrong rises, he comes, age after age, to protect the good. So Rama and Krishna aren't rivals, or two gods to choose between. For Vaishnavas they're one Lord, Vishnu, come again. An old servant of Rama knew him in the dark. It's why many homes keep Rama and Krishna on the same shelf.
screen: `THE JEWEL GOES MISSING.` · `HE DOESN'T ARGUE. HE FINDS OUT.` · `JAMBAVAN KNOWS HIS LORD.` · `AVATARA: GOD COMES AGAIN.` · then, large: `RAMA AND KRISHNA: ONE LORD.`

segments.voice: Bring two images to mind: Rama with his bow, and Krishna with his flute. Let them sit side by side, the way they share a shelf in many homes, and Many Hindus sing an old chant that holds both names in one breath: Hare Rama, Hare Krishna. If you pray, say it slowly a few times, or simply say the two names, Rama, Krishna, as one prayer; if you don't, rest with the thought that what is good can come back into the world again and again.
Syamantaka, the jewel the sun gave Satrajit, and the rumor it caused in Dwaraka. Today, a bear in a cave who knew Krishna as his Lord Rama, come again.
Your line: one Lord, come again as Rama and Krishna. Jambavan knew him in the dark. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Many Hindu homes and temples keep Rama and Krishna side by side as forms of Vishnu; the Syamantaka story is told in Bhagavata recitations, and in some regions it is read or heard on Ganesh Chaturthi, as a story about false accusation and how it is cleared.
